description.narrative: Core support to the Bolivian environmental NGO Fundación Amigos de la Naturaleza for conservation of ecosystems and biodiversity
Kärnstöd till den bolivianska miljö-NGOn Fundación Amigos de la Naturaleza för bevarande av ekosystem och biologisk mångfald

FANs Institutional Strategic Plan 2021-2026 proposes a strategic response to the environmental impacts and the violation of the livelihoods of the most fragile populations due to the implementation in Bolivia of an economic model based on the degradation of natural resources and the environment. In this sense, FANs vision is as follows:
'To ensure that as a society Bolivians assume that the conservation of Nature is the fundamental basis for achieving an integral and sustainable development.'
The Strategic Plan 2021-2025 has set-up the following strategic objectives:
Strategic objective 1: 'Contributing to an effective and inclusive conservation and sustainable management of forests and biodiversity in key landscapes for ecosystem connectivity and functionality'
Strategic objective 2: 'Promoting the adoption of sustainable production alternatives that improves the ecological footprint and improve the livelihoods of indigenous and rural populations.'
Strategic objective 3): 'Encouraging climate action and strategies based on scientific evidence to face climate change and its impacts on public development agendas.'
Strategic objective 4): 'Strengthening the governance and territorial management to attain safer, more resilient, inclusive, and sustainable communities and cities.'

FAN's results and achivements 2023/2024: FAN has continued to implement their Institutional Strategic Plan 2021-2026, which this contribution aims to support - in form of a core support. This includes strengthening alliances with FANs strategic partners, as well as with financial partners, in order to contribute to the conservation of natural heritage and the environmental functions that sustain the livelihoods and well-being of its population for sustainable development and climate resilience.
Some highlights of the results achieved during 2023 are:
- Launching of the AMA platform, the first geoviewer of maps and data from the RAISG for the monitoring of forest fires and deforestation in the Amazon with real-time forest fire alert information through the detection and reporting of heat sources, with its own data that are generated and processed under methodological standards common to the countries that are part of the Amazon. As well as the generation of the first collection of annual maps on land cover and land use change in Bolivia through the MapBiomas Platform, which contains maps and statistics on the dynamics of annual land cover and land use change in the country at different scales in the period 1985-2021.
- Identification of 17 Tropical Important Plant Areas (TIPAs) of the Inter-Andean Dry Valleys of Bolivia identified, mapped and documented.
- Developed capacities in productive restoration in 4 Chiquitano indigenous communities by establishing pilot models with the community members in degraded areas with silvopastoral systems and agroforestry systems (SAF) that include Chiquitano almonds, as well as areas of natural plant regeneration. And, supporting the development of products based on Chiquitano almonds, pesoé- , copaibo- and totaí oil and the development of promotional material and commercial image of 5 associations of the Chiquitano indigenous communities.
- Technically supported the development Forest Emissions Reference Level (NREF) version 3.0 to comply with UNFCCC standards, which serves as a baseline against the emission reductions that can be measured and what results-based contributions can be accomplished, aligning with the ART/TREES standard for prioritized jurisdictions. This component has been crucial to make Bolivia eligible for receiving climate funding. FAN strengthened the skills and capacities of a technical team of 10 technical specialists (20% women) who are part of the MRV (monitoring, report and verification) team at the Forestry Directorate of the Bolivian Ministry of Environment and Water.
- In 2023, FAN strengthened capacities for the prevention, preparedness, and response to forest fires in 38 indigenous and peasant communities, through the training and equipping of communal forest fire brigades and the implementation of an early warning and response system articulated to local coordination mechanisms. More than 1,200 people (38% women) were reached through training, technical assistance and exchanges of experiences aimed at establishing better fire management practices, which include the analysis, mapping and participatory monitoring of the territory and fire risks with the use of ICT, planning of controlled burns, early warning and combatting forest fires. FAN also provided technical assistance and equipment to strengthen the management of forest fires in 6 national and subnational protected areas (Noel Kempff Mercado National Park, Otuquis National Park, San Matías IMN, and the UCPN Tucabaca, Santa Cruz la Vieja and Concepción Lagoon).
During 2024 there was record breaking wildfires due to severe and prolonged drought. 12.6 million hectares burned nationwide, with:57% (7.1 million ha) in forested areas. 43% (5.4 million ha) in nonforested/agricultural areas. Santa Cruz department was the most affected:8.8 million ha burned, with 81% in forests. 4.2 million ha burned within protected areas, representing 48% of the regions total burned area.
FAN's results and achivements 2024/2025:
Continued implementation of the Strategic Institutional Plan 2021-2026.
OUTCOME 1: CONSERVATION, FIRE PREVENTION AND CLIMATE CHANGE ADAPTATION AND MITIGATION: -Strengthened fire prevention and management in six protected areas in Santa Cruz. -Updated Management Plan for Otuquis National Park, the first in Bolivia to formally integrate Integrated Fire Management. -Supported four municipal governments with risk management tools and contingency plans. -Trained 58 communities in fire management across Chiquitania, Pantanal, and Northern Amazon. -Assisted two municipalities in drafting disaster risk management laws. -Continued rigorous work in socioenvironmental monitoring, with the second collection of MapBiomas Bolivia (19852023)
OUTCOME 2 SUSTAINABLE PRODUCTION MODELS: -Strengthened value chains for forest products (e.g., almendra chiquitana, copaibo, asaí) that benefited indigenous communities in Santa Cruz and Beni. -Promoted sustainable management of 110,421 ha of native Chiquitano forest. -Introduced agroforestry and regenerative soil practices in indigenous communities. -Formed alliances with the private sector, notably with Cooltiva and its platform Conectando el campo y la cocina to link small producers with the gastronomy sector. -Supported the Santa Cruz Apiculture Law to protect bees and promote beekeeping.
OUTCOME 3 ENVIRONMENTAL GOVERNANCE: -Approval of the Departamental Policy on Integrated Fire Management and its implementation strategy, promulgated by promulgated by the Autonomous Departmental Government of Santa Cruz. -Contributed to the third version of the Forest Emissions Reference Level (FREL). -Expanded the network of Permanent Measurement Plots (PMM) for biomass. In 2024, 36 new plots were installed: 24 plots in the department of Santa Cruz, 11 in Pando, and 1 in Beni. -Helped 14 TacanaCavineño communities develop communal regulations for resource use. -Supported indigenous organizations in creating norms for nontimber forest product access and conflict resolution.
OUTCOME 4 GENDER: -Strengthened leadership of 71 indigenous women in environmental and productive roles. -Trained 352 women in sustainable forest product management, climate resilience, and gender/youth inclusion.
